# C1 — Redundant Computation

*Level 1 card. 8 root causes. Open the level-2 card before accepting any of them.*

Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged. This includes code whose results are never consumed (dead code, resultless computation), operations that repeat work already done in the same scope (repeated computation, redundant assignments), setup and initialization on paths where results are unused (unnecessary initialization), excessive invocation of runtime housekeeping (GC calls, unchecked logging), and intermediate variables that add overhead without improving clarity. The common thread is that removing or simplifying these operations would not change program behavior but would reduce energy consumption.

## Root causes in this category

| ID | Name | Looks for | The repair | Measurable? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | a value computed and bound to a name that nothing ever reads | delete the computation whose result nothing reads | yes, scales with input |
| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | a store that leaves the program's state exactly as it already was | delete the assignment that leaves state unchanged | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | a branch whose outcome is the same whichever way it goes | delete the control flow that cannot change the outcome | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | the same value computed twice in one scope, where one local would serve both | compute the value once, bind it, and read the binding | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | a computation run in full whose result nothing downstream actually needs | delete the computation whose result nothing consumes | yes, scales with input |
| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | setup done unconditionally that only one path actually needs | move the setup inside the branch that needs it | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | a name bound, read exactly once, and never needed again | inline the single-use temporary | yes, scales with call count |
| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | runtime housekeeping invoked far more often than anything needs it | remove the housekeeping call, or defer the work until it is known to be needed | yes, scales with call count |

## If nothing here fits

Say so and move on. Reporting a weak match from a category you have already opened is the most common way this analysis goes wrong: the category is open because something drew you here, which is not the same as a smell being present.
